title: The God Who Wants to Dwell

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God. They will know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of Egypt so that I might dwell among them. I am the Lord their God." - Exodus 29:45-46 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is where all of it has been heading. After chapters of measurements, garments, and sacrifices, God states the purpose in the simplest words: "I will dwell among them... and be their God." Everything — the tabernacle, the priesthood, the offerings — existed so that God could live among His people.

And notice the astonishing reframing of the exodus. God says He brought them out of Egypt "so that I might dwell among them." The rescue was not the goal; nearness was the goal. He did not free them merely to make them comfortable or independent. He freed them so He could be with them.

That is still His purpose. Salvation is not simply rescue from judgment; it is rescue into relationship. Jesus came and tabernacled among us (John 1:14), the Spirit now dwells within us (1 Cor 3:16), and Scripture ends with God's dwelling place among His people forever, God Himself with them as their God (Rev 21:3). Every chapter of this long section serves that single sentence. God wants to be with you. That is the whole point.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I see salvation mainly as rescue from something, or rescue into relationship with God?
What difference does it make today that God's deepest desire is to be with me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You rescued me not only from judgment but into relationship with Yourself. Thank You that Your deepest desire is to dwell with me. Let me live conscious of Your nearness. Amen.
